Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
1 October 2026 .
· Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 BREAKING: news.antiwar.com reports three ships were struck in the Strait of Hormuz and the IRGC says the US is not responding to attacks; not independently confirmed.

02 IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the oil price feed is currently down.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remained under severe pressure on 30 September, with multiple tanker strikes adding to an already critical throughput picture. news.antiwar.com reports three ships were struck in the strait and that the IRGC stated the US is not responding to the attacks; that claim has not been carried by a major wire in this feed. The Maritime Executive reports three vessels were struck in the strait as Iran's grip on traffic loosens. These reports follow the 28 September strike on the Kuwaiti supertanker Al Funtas and the 23 September death of a seafarer aboard the bulk carrier Cape Dao; neither incident is being treated as new here. On the diplomatic track, Iran says it is reviewing the US ceasefire counterproposal, with Strait of Hormuz terms still unpublished, a development carried in yesterday's brief with no new material facts added in this window. CNBC reports crude oil exports through the strait have hit prewar levels but notes fuel shipments remain constrained and that the recovery depends on US military protection of tankers. CENTCOM says it has redirected 125 commercial vessels since Iran reimposed its maritime blockade, per trend.az. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The oil price feed has not produced a print in over two hours. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, easing over 24 hours, flagged low-confidence because two of its inputs are stale or missing (the Brent-WTI forward spread and Manifold forward contracts), with Kalshi forward contracts as its top contributor.
